requirements_summary: Private (air-gapped) deployment evaluation. Workloads are PHI-adjacent (clinical note summarization + patient communications). Needs strong separation of duties: Security admin can manage SSO, view/export audit logs, and review authz decisions; Platform ops can manage cluster/runtime settings; Developers can deploy prompts/apps but cannot manage org-wide settings; Billing admin isolated. Must support SAML/SSO with group-to-role mapping. Audit logging must include actor identity, role(s), decision allow/deny, and policy version; export to SIEM with retention controls. notes:
Account: Northstar Health (enterprise provider network). Private deployment only; procurement flagged from day 1: "no SaaS control plane dependency" and "no outbound internet" from their environment.

Current stance:
- They like Redwood runtime performance + operational tooling, but they’re holding the line on RBAC v2 maturity for Private.
- Quote from deep dive: "We can’t give our app teams Org Admin just so they can rotate a key or view logs. We need true least privilege and an audit trail we can show to compliance." (paraphrased)

Key evaluation asks (RBAC v2 / roles):
- Default roles aren’t enough for them; they want at least one custom role for Security Ops.
- They specifically want:
  - A role that can view/export audit logs + view authz failures/denies (for investigations)
  - But cannot touch billing, API keys, or model rollout controls
- Separation of duties requirements were repeated multiple times (Security vs Billing vs Platform Ops).

Air-gapped policy updates:
- They will require a signed policy bundle artifact and an offline update mechanism (ideally tied to their standard upgrade window).
- They asked: what happens if policy bundle version differs from control plane version? Need a crisp answer for version skew.
- They asked for rollback guidance: how to revert a bad policy bundle quickly without opening up broader access.

SSO/SAML:
- Uses enterprise IdP with group-based entitlements. They want documented mapping guidance and recommended group structure.
- Concern: group churn/latency (how quickly role changes take effect; any caching; how to force invalidation).

Audit logging / evidence:
- Wants sample audit log events showing authz decision context (allow/deny + reason codes + policy version + role IDs) for their SIEM team to validate.
- Asked about retention controls and whether audit export can be restricted to Security-only.

Commercial:
- They’re penciling a pilot starting after RBAC v2 is available in their private build and policy update story is validated.
- ARR range expectation came from them: mid six figures if we meet security requirements and pilot meets latency.

Internal coordination:
- Pull in Marcus Lin (Security exec owner) for next call; they asked for a direct security point-of-contact.
- Vivek Kulkarni to confirm private policy distribution approach + timeline; Markus Klein to keep driving technical alignment.

Artifacts referenced in meetings:

- Internal notes on private policy distribution: drive://shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/rbac-v2-private-policy-distribution

Open questions to resolve with them:
- Do they need on-prem HSM integration immediately or is KMS sufficient in phase 1?
- Expected latency/throughput targets by use case (they gave qualitative: "near real-time for clinician workflows"; need numbers).
- Whether they’ll accept a phased approach: default roles at pilot start, custom roles shortly after (they sounded skeptical; may require at least one custom role at pilot start).
